sources.title: Pro Git Book — Recording Changes to the Repository
Pro Git Book — Basic Branching and Merging
Pro Git Book — Working with Remotes

summary: A practical introduction to Git for new developers, built around the small, consistent mental model that makes day-to-day Git click: a working tree, a staging area, and a committed history, with branches as cheap pointers that move through it. The lesson starts a repository from scratch with git init and via git clone, covers the modern default branch name main, then walks through the edit-stage-commit cycle using git status, git add, git diff, and git commit, including how to write small focused commits and a sensible .gitignore. It introduces branches with git switch and git switch -c, explains the three remote-syncing commands fetch, pull, and push (including the -u upstream flag and the diverged-branch pull.ff and pull.rebase settings), shows how fast-forward and three-way merges differ, and walks through reading and resolving conflict markers with git merge --abort as the safety net. It closes with a simple GitHub Flow style workflow — branch off main, commit, push, open a pull request, review, merge, delete the branch, pull main back down — and a ten-command cheat sheet to commit to memory.
